title: Depth Anything V2
abstract: Presents an improved monocular depth estimation foundation model achieving finer and more robust predictions through three strategies: replacing labeled real images with synthetic images, scaling up the teacher model capacity, and teaching student models via large-scale pseudo-labeled real images. Models range from 25M to 1.3B parameters and are significantly more efficient than Stable Diffusion-based competitors. Metric depth variants and a new evaluation benchmark with diverse, precisely-annotated scenes are also provided.
relevance_note: State-of-the-art monocular depth foundation model with small variants deployable at real-time FPS on embedded hardware, directly relevant to camera-only depth sensing on Jetson Orin Nano.

title: Depth Anything: Unleashing the Power of Large-Scale Unlabeled Data
abstract: Introduces a practical monocular depth estimation foundation model designed for robust performance across diverse images and conditions. The authors scale their dataset using a data engine that collected and automatically annotated approximately 62 million unlabeled images. Two strategies improve generalisation: more challenging optimization targets via data augmentation and auxiliary supervision from pre-trained semantic encoders. Demonstrates strong zero-shot generalisation across six public datasets and state-of-the-art results when fine-tuned for metric depth.
relevance_note: Foundational predecessor to Depth Anything V2; establishes the large-scale unlabeled-data training paradigm that enables lightweight variants suitable for indoor wheelchair perception.

title: Towards Robust Monocular Depth Estimation: Mixing Datasets for Zero-shot Cross-dataset Transfer
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (TPAMI)
abstract: Develops methods to combine multiple depth estimation datasets during training despite incompatible annotations, using a robust training objective invariant to changes in depth range and scale and employing multi-objective learning. Using five diverse datasets including 3D films as a novel source, the approach achieves superior performance through zero-shot cross-dataset evaluation, demonstrating that mixing complementary data sources greatly improves monocular depth estimation. Forms the basis of the widely-used MiDaS depth model.
relevance_note: MiDaS is a widely-deployed baseline monocular depth model used in indoor robotics, providing zero-shot generalisation across scene types relevant to indoor wheelchair navigation.

title: Vision Transformers for Dense Prediction
abstract: Presents dense vision transformers (DPT) that replace convolutional backbones for dense prediction tasks. The architecture assembles tokens from multiple transformer stages into multi-resolution representations, then progressively refines them using a convolutional decoder. Provides constant high resolution processing and global receptive fields at every stage. Demonstrates up to 28% relative improvement on monocular depth estimation and sets a new state of the art on ADE20K semantic segmentation with 49.02% mIoU.
relevance_note: DPT is the backbone of MiDaS v3 and Depth Anything; understanding its architecture is essential for deploying and optimising monocular depth on the Jetson Orin Nano.

title: AdaBins: Depth Estimation Using Adaptive Bins
abstract: Introduces a transformer-based architecture block that divides the depth range into bins whose center value is estimated adaptively per image, with final depth values estimated as linear combinations of the bin centers. The method is built on an EfficientNet-B5 encoder with a standard decoder and a mini-ViT module for global context. Achieves decisive improvements over the state of the art on NYU Depth v2 and KITTI with a 21% reduction in relative absolute error on NYU.
relevance_note: AdaBins achieves strong metric depth accuracy on the NYU indoor dataset, making it a relevant baseline for indoor depth estimation in the wheelchair context.

title: ZoeDepth: Zero-shot Transfer by Combining Relative and Metric Depth
abstract: Proposes the first approach combining both relative and metric depth estimation, using pre-training on 12 datasets for relative depth followed by fine-tuning on metric datasets. A lightweight head with a novel metric bins module is used per domain, with automatic image routing via a latent classifier. The flagship model ZoeD-M12-NK achieves a 21% improvement in relative absolute error on NYU Depth v2 and strong zero-shot generalisation across eight unseen indoor and outdoor datasets.
relevance_note: ZoeDepth produces metric (absolute) depth from a single image with zero-shot generalisation to new indoor scenes, directly applicable to obstacle ranging in a wheelchair context without LiDAR.

title: RAFT-Stereo: Multilevel Recurrent Field Transforms for Stereo Matching
abstract: Presents RAFT-Stereo, a deep learning architecture for stereo matching built upon the RAFT optical flow framework. Key innovations include multi-level convolutional GRUs that enhance information propagation across image scales. A real-time variant is available by adjusting the GRU hierarchy. Achieves top performance on Middlebury with significantly better 1-pixel error rates and superior results on ETH3D. More memory efficient than competing approaches, enabling full-resolution stereo on megapixel images.
relevance_note: RAFT-Stereo is a strong learned stereo method with configurable speed/accuracy trade-offs, suitable for real-time depth from stereo cameras (ZED Mini, OAK-D) on a Jetson-class device.

title: Iterative Geometry Encoding Volume for Stereo Matching
abstract: Introduces IGEV-Stereo, which constructs a geometry encoding volume incorporating geometry, context, and local matching information, and iteratively indexes it to update the disparity map. Uses the geometry encoding volume to regress an accurate starting point for ConvGRU iterations, accelerating convergence. Ranked first on KITTI 2015 and 2012 (Reflective) benchmarks among published methods while being the fastest among the top-10 approaches. Demonstrates strong cross-dataset generalisation.
relevance_note: IGEV-Stereo achieves the best accuracy-speed trade-off in learned stereo matching, making it a prime candidate for real-time stereo depth from the ZED Mini or OAK-D on the Jetson Orin Nano.

title: Practical Stereo Matching via Cascaded Recurrent Network with Adaptive Correlation
abstract: Proposes CREStereo, addressing practical stereo matching via a hierarchical network with recurrent refinement updating disparities coarse-to-fine, plus a stacked cascaded architecture for inference. Introduces an adaptive group correlation layer to handle imperfect image rectification, and a new synthetic dataset with difficult cases for better real-world generalisation. Achieves first-place rankings on both Middlebury and ETH3D benchmarks while demonstrating high-quality results on real-world photographs.
relevance_note: CREStereo handles imperfect rectification robustly, which is relevant when deploying consumer stereo cameras like the ZED Mini or OAK-D in uncontrolled indoor environments.

title: ORB-SLAM3: An Accurate Open-Source Library for Visual, Visual-Inertial and Multi-Map SLAM
abstract: Presents ORB-SLAM3, the first system able to perform visual, visual-inertial and multi-map SLAM with monocular, stereo and RGB-D cameras using pin-hole and fisheye lens models. Integrates a tightly-coupled visual-inertial system using Maximum-a-Posteriori estimation and a multiple map system with improved place recognition. Achieves 2 to 5 times more accurate results than previous approaches, with stereo-inertial SLAM reaching 3.6 cm average accuracy on EuRoC. Tracking thread operates at 30-40 FPS.
relevance_note: ORB-SLAM3 is the leading open-source SLAM library supporting RGB-D and stereo modes at real-time FPS, directly applicable to indoor localisation and mapping for a shared-autonomy wheelchair.

title: RTAB-Map as an Open-Source Lidar and Visual SLAM Library for Large-Scale and Long-Term Online Operation
abstract: Describes RTAB-Map, an RGB-D, stereo and lidar graph-based SLAM approach using an incremental appearance-based loop closure detector with a bag-of-words model. A memory management approach limits locations used for loop closure detection and graph optimisation to maintain real-time constraints in large-scale environments. Provides comprehensive quantitative and qualitative comparison across KITTI, EuRoC, TUM RGB-D, and MIT Stata Center datasets, outlining strengths and limitations of various sensor configurations for autonomous navigation.
relevance_note: RTAB-Map is a production-ready RGB-D SLAM framework with ROS integration and real-time loop closure, widely used in indoor mobile robotics and directly applicable to wheelchair navigation.

title: Kimera: An Open-Source Library for Real-Time Metric-Semantic Localization and Mapping
abstract: Presents Kimera, a C++ library enabling simultaneous localisation, mapping, and 3D semantic understanding in real-time. The system combines visual-inertial odometry for state estimation with pose graph optimisation, mesh reconstruction, and semantic labelling. Runs in real-time on a CPU and produces a 3D metric-semantic mesh by processing semantically labelled images. The modular design allows independent or integrated operation of components, functioning as a visual-inertial odometer or complete SLAM system.
relevance_note: Kimera provides real-time semantic 3D mesh maps from camera+IMU data on CPU, enabling obstacle-aware navigation for a wheelchair without LiDAR.

title: OpenVINS: A Research Platform for Visual-Inertial Estimation
abstract: Presents OpenVINS, an open platform for visual-inertial estimation research. The core filter is an Extended Kalman filter fusing inertial information with sparse visual feature tracks using the Multi-State Constraint Kalman Filter (MSCKF) sliding window formulation. Features include on-manifold sliding window Kalman filter, online camera intrinsic and extrinsic calibration, camera-to-IMU time offset calibration, SLAM landmarks with consistent FEJ treatments, modular state management, and an extendable VI simulator with evaluation toolbox.
relevance_note: OpenVINS is a lightweight visual-inertial odometry framework suitable for edge deployment with stereo or monocular cameras and IMU, providing accurate indoor localisation for a wheelchair without LiDAR.

title: NeRF-SLAM: Real-Time Dense Monocular SLAM with Neural Radiance Fields
abstract: Proposes a novel geometric and photometric 3D mapping pipeline for accurate real-time scene reconstruction from monocular images by integrating dense monocular SLAM with neural radiance fields. Uses uncertainty-based depth loss to achieve both photometric and geometric accuracy. Outperforms competing approaches with improvements up to 179% in PSNR and 86% in depth accuracy while operating in real-time using only monocular images.
relevance_note: Demonstrates real-time dense 3D map building from a single monocular camera using NeRF, a promising camera-only alternative to depth cameras for indoor scene reconstruction.

title: RAFT: Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transforms for Optical Flow
abstract: Presents RAFT, a deep network for optical flow estimation that extracts per-pixel features, constructs multi-scale correlation volumes comparing all pixel pairs, and iteratively refines flow predictions using a recurrent mechanism. On KITTI achieves 5.10% F1-all error, a 16% improvement over prior best. On Sintel final pass achieves 2.855 pixel end-point-error, a 30% improvement. The lightweight update operator has only 2.7M parameters. A smaller RAFT-S variant is available for faster edge inference.
relevance_note: RAFT is the dominant learned optical flow method with a compact small variant, enabling motion detection of dynamic objects (people, other wheelchairs) from camera frames in indoor scenes.

title: LiteFlowNet: A Lightweight Convolutional Neural Network for Optical Flow Estimation
abstract: Introduces LiteFlowNet as a more efficient alternative to FlowNet2 for optical flow estimation, outperforming it on Sintel and KITTI benchmarks while being 30 times smaller and 1.36 times faster. Key innovations include a lightweight cascaded network with improved inference at each pyramid level, a novel flow regularisation layer using feature-driven local convolution, and pyramidal feature extraction with feature warping rather than image warping. LiteFlowNet2 (TPAMI 2020) further improves accuracy by up to 23.3% with 2.2x faster runtime.
relevance_note: LiteFlowNet is specifically designed for low-parameter, fast optical flow, making it well-suited for detecting dynamic obstacles on the compute-constrained Jetson Orin Nano.

title: PWC-Net: CNNs for Optical Flow Using Pyramid, Warping, and Cost Volume
abstract: Introduces PWC-Net, a lightweight CNN for optical flow that combines three classical principles—pyramid structures, warping, and cost volumes—into a learnable framework. Uses feature pyramids and warps second-image features based on current flow estimates, then constructs partial cost volumes for refinement. PWC-Net is 17 times smaller than FlowNet2, achieves state-of-the-art results on MPI Sintel and KITTI 2015, and runs at approximately 35 fps on standard resolution images.
relevance_note: PWC-Net is a compact, real-time optical flow network that can detect dynamic pedestrians and obstacles in indoor scenes on embedded hardware.

title: SMOKE: Single-Stage Monocular 3D Object Detection via Keypoint Estimation
abstract: Proposes SMOKE, which predicts a 3D bounding box for each detected object by combining a single keypoint estimate with regressed 3D variables, eliminating the redundant 2D detection network. Introduces a multi-step disentangling approach for constructing 3D bounding boxes, improving training convergence and detection accuracy. Does not require pre/post-processing or a refinement stage. Achieves state-of-the-art on KITTI for monocular 3D detection with ~30ms runtime on a single GPU.
relevance_note: SMOKE is an efficient single-stage monocular 3D detection baseline, demonstrating that camera-only 3D bounding boxes are feasible for real-time detection of obstacles in a wheelchair context.

title: FCOS3D: Fully Convolutional One-Stage Monocular 3D Object Detection
abstract: Proposes a fully convolutional one-stage monocular 3D detection framework that transforms 3D targets into the image domain and decouples them as 2D and 3D components. Objects are distributed across feature levels based on 2D scales with training assignments based on projected 3D centres. Redefines centre-ness using a 2D Gaussian distribution aligned with the 3D-centre formulation. Achieved first place among all vision-only methods in the nuScenes 3D detection challenge of NeurIPS 2020.
relevance_note: FCOS3D is the dominant single-camera 3D detection framework, establishing how 3D positions can be predicted from a monocular stream for camera-only obstacle detection in a wheelchair.

title: BEVDet: High-performance Multi-camera 3D Object Detection in Bird-Eye-View
abstract: Introduces BEVDet, a camera-only 3D detection paradigm that lifts image features to bird's-eye-view for autonomous driving applications. The modular framework reuses existing image-view encoders, a view transformer, BEV encoder, and task-specific head, and introduces specialised data augmentation and improved non-maximum suppression. BEVDet-Tiny achieves 31.2% mAP at 15.6 FPS with 11% of the computational budget of heavier models; BEVDet-Base reaches 39.3% mAP, significantly exceeding all published results at the time.
relevance_note: BEVDet demonstrates camera-only occupancy-style 3D perception through BEV lifting, providing a pathway toward pure-camera obstacle maps for indoor wheelchair navigation.

title: Efficient RGB-D Semantic Segmentation for Indoor Scene Analysis
abstract: Presents ESANet (Efficient Scene Analysis Network), an RGB-D segmentation method optimisable through NVIDIA TensorRT for real-time performance on mobile robot platforms. Tests on NYUv2 and SUNRGB-D indoor datasets demonstrate competitive performance with faster inference than existing methods. Validated on outdoor scenes using Cityscapes data. Practical results from indoor robotic applications show the approach enables person detection, free space identification, mapping, and navigation on a Jetson AGX Xavier.
relevance_note: ESANet provides real-time RGB-D semantic segmentation validated on a Jetson Xavier, enabling indoor free-space and person detection directly applicable to a camera-equipped wheelchair.

title: ByteTrack: Multi-Object Tracking by Associating Every Detection Box
abstract: Presents ByteTrack, a multi-object tracking method that associates almost every detection box including low-confidence ones, rather than discarding occluded objects. For low-confidence detections, the method uses similarity with existing tracklets to recover true objects and filter background noise. Achieves 80.3 MOTA, 77.3 IDF1, and 63.1 HOTA on MOT17 at 30 FPS on a V100. Demonstrates consistent improvement across nine state-of-the-art trackers with IDF1 gains of 1-10 points.
relevance_note: ByteTrack is the leading real-time multi-object tracker for maintaining consistent person tracks in indoor scenes, essential for a wheelchair to track and avoid dynamic human obstacles.

title: BoT-SORT: Robust Associations Multi-Pedestrian Tracking
abstract: Presents BoT-SORT combining motion and appearance information with camera-motion compensation and a more accurate Kalman filter state vector. Camera motion compensation employs global motion compensation via affine transformations using pyramidal Lucas-Kanade optical flow and RANSAC-based outlier rejection. Achieves 80.5 MOTA, 80.2 IDF1, and 65.0 HOTA on MOT17, ranking first on MOTChallenge on both MOT17 and MOT20 test sets.
relevance_note: BoT-SORT adds re-ID and camera-motion compensation to ByteTrack, providing robust pedestrian tracking under camera movement and occlusion in wheelchair indoor navigation scenarios.

title: Lightweight Multimodal Domain Generic Person Reidentification Metric for Person-Following Robots
abstract: Presents a metric that learns deep cross-representations to address pose, viewpoint, and illumination variations while tackling impostors and style changes for person-following robots. Combines a lightweight CNN backbone with a part-wise attention mechanism for domain-generic indoor and outdoor re-identification. Achieves 80.73% and 64.44% Rank-1 identification on PRID and VIPeR datasets in complex multi-modal open-set scenarios where appearance changes significantly across domains.
relevance_note: Directly addresses re-identification for person-following robots with a lightweight model, enabling a wheelchair to persistently identify and track the user or nearby pedestrians.

title: Monocular Occupancy Prediction for Scalable Indoor Scenes
abstract: Presents ISO, a method for estimating 3D occupancy in indoor environments from single RGB images. Leverages a pre-trained depth predictor and introduces the Dual Feature Line of Sight Projection (D-FLoSP) module to enhance voxel feature learning. Releases Occ-ScanNet, a large-scale occupancy benchmark 40 times larger than NYUv2, enabling scalable indoor scene research. Results demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on both NYUv2 and Occ-ScanNet benchmarks.
relevance_note: ISO directly addresses indoor 3D occupancy prediction from a monocular camera, providing the voxel-level free-space maps needed for safe wheelchair navigation without LiDAR.

title: Indoor Navigation Assistance for Visually Impaired People via Dynamic SLAM and Panoptic Segmentation with an RGB-D Sensor
abstract: Presents an assistive technology for visually impaired indoor navigation using an RGB-D sensor. Applies panoptic segmentation to identify potential dynamic objects (people), estimates user positioning via feature point extraction and depth, and distinguishes and monitors dynamic obstacles after ego-motion estimation. Determines dynamic obstacle positions and velocities, communicating hazards to users through acoustic signals. Demonstrates robust dynamic object tracking in real indoor environments.
relevance_note: Directly demonstrates dynamic SLAM with panoptic segmentation for indoor assistive navigation using an RGB-D camera, closely analogous to the wheelchair perception pipeline.

title: Real-time Monocular Depth Estimation on Embedded Systems
abstract: Proposes RT-MonoDepth and RT-MonoDepth-S, two lightweight neural network architectures achieving competitive depth accuracy while enabling real-time processing on embedded platforms. RT-MonoDepth achieves 18.4 FPS on NVIDIA Jetson Nano and 253.0 FPS on Jetson AGX Orin using 640x192 RGB images. RT-MonoDepth-S achieves 30.5 FPS on Jetson Nano and 364.1 FPS on AGX Orin, demonstrating superior speed over existing fast monocular depth methods on KITTI.
relevance_note: RT-MonoDepth is specifically benchmarked on Jetson hardware and achieves real-time depth estimation, making it the most directly relevant monocular depth model for Jetson Orin Nano deployment.

title: Benchmarking Deep Learning Models for Object Detection on Edge Computing Devices
abstract: Evaluates several state-of-the-art object detection models (YOLOv8 variants, EfficientDet Lite, SSD) on resource-constrained edge devices including Raspberry Pi and Jetson Orin Nano. Measures energy consumption, inference speed, and accuracy. Key findings indicate lower-accuracy models offer better energy efficiency, while the Jetson Orin Nano delivered the fastest processing despite highest idle consumption. Emphasises the importance of balancing accuracy, speed, and energy when selecting models for edge deployment.
relevance_note: Provides empirical benchmarks of object detection models directly on the Jetson Orin Nano, informing model selection for the indoor wheelchair perception pipeline.

title: Vision-Based Mobile Robotics Obstacle Avoidance With Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Presents an end-to-end deep learning approach where robots navigate using only monocular camera input, learning directly from raw images to generate movement commands. Finds that discrete action spaces perform better than continuous controls in maze environments, and improves learning efficiency by incorporating depth predictions from generative adversarial networks. Demonstrates effective camera-only obstacle avoidance in indoor environments without explicit mapping.
relevance_note: Demonstrates camera-only end-to-end obstacle avoidance for indoor mobile robots using DRL, providing an alternative learning-based paradigm for the wheelchair perception-to-action pipeline.

title: Empirical Comparison of Four Stereoscopic Depth Sensing Cameras for Robotics Applications
abstract: Evaluates four stereoscopic RGB-D cameras (Intel RealSense D435, D455, StereoLabs ZED 2, Luxonis OAK-D Pro) across three test scenarios (planar surfaces, plastic dolls, household objects) using over 3,000 frames per camera. Finds the D435 best for close-range table-top robotics with sub-1cm error, while ZED 2 maintains accuracy within 3cm at 4-meter distances but requires external GPU processing. The OAK-D Pro offers integrated AI inference capabilities. All 12,000+ frames are publicly available.
relevance_note: Provides direct empirical evidence on the performance of the exact cameras (RealSense D435, OAK-D Pro) being considered for the wheelchair, informing sensor selection for the vision pipeline.

title: CoNav Chair: Design of a ROS-based Smart Wheelchair for Shared Control Navigation in the Built Environment
abstract: Presents a ROS-based smart wheelchair incorporating shared control navigation and obstacle avoidance, balancing autonomous features with user control to support people with disabilities. Hardware integrates LiDAR, RGB-D camera, IMU, and encoders for comprehensive situational awareness. Software uses RTAB-Map for 3D mapping with the RGB-D sensor as primary input. Shared control framework integrates user inputs with autonomous navigation. Demonstrates significantly fewer collisions and comparable task completion time versus full autonomy or full manual modes.
relevance_note: Directly demonstrates a shared-autonomy wheelchair system using RGB-D-based RTAB-Map SLAM, providing the closest system-level reference for the proposed wheelchair perception pipeline.

title: Driving Assistance System with Obstacle Avoidance for Electric Wheelchairs
abstract: Presents technology enabling conversion of manual wheelchairs into electric models with a detachable driving module and specialised algorithm. Integrates the dynamic window approach for obstacle avoidance, employing sensors for environmental perception. Evaluates potential movements within velocity space to determine optimal paths for real-time safe navigation. Testing demonstrates successful collision prevention in indoor environments while maintaining user joystick control, enhancing maneuverability for individuals with limited mobility.
relevance_note: Directly addresses sensor-based obstacle avoidance for electric wheelchairs in indoor environments, providing a system-level reference for integrating perception with wheelchair motion control.

title: iELAS: An ELAS-Based Energy-Efficient Accelerator for Real-Time Stereo Matching on FPGA Platform
abstract: Presents a specialised hardware design for executing the ELAS stereo vision algorithm efficiently on FPGA devices. Reforms the computationally demanding triangulation component into a more hardware-suitable structure using point interpolation. Optimisations focus on memory handling, parallel processing, and instruction pipelining. Results demonstrate up to 38.4x and 3.32x frame rate improvement compared to Intel i7 processors and alternative FPGA implementations respectively, with corresponding energy efficiency gains on the KITTI dataset.
relevance_note: Provides a hardware-accelerated ELAS stereo implementation, relevant as an ultra-low-power alternative to learned stereo methods for real-time depth on embedded wheelchair hardware.
